entries.providerBehavior: GitLab can report more than one pipeline for one commit (a branch pipeline and a merge-request pipeline) instead of a single pipeline.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: read-pipeline-run for the commit returns every reported pipeline, each with a distinct identity, closed-set job states, and trace evidence where the provider records a trace; no newest-wins singleton is selected.

entries.providerBehavior: GitLab merge status resolves asynchronously: values such as checking and unchecked mean the provider has not finished evaluating mergeability.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Asynchronous native values normalize to non-terminal delivery review states only; they never report merged or closed while the native value is still evaluating.

entries.providerBehavior: GitLab may report merge_status and detailed_merge_status simultaneously with different meanings.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: detailed_merge_status is authoritative when present and merge_status is the fallback; an unknown native value fails visibly instead of silently flattening to a delivery state.

entries.providerBehavior: A GitLab non-2xx response is built without a structured status, so an authorization rejection is not distinguishable from a transport failure.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: read-delivery-request resolves to tracker.transport.failed and the failure owns no httpStatus property; the difference is recorded as failure-classification.

entries.providerBehavior: A GitLab transport rejection produces no provider response at all.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: read-delivery-request resolves to tracker.transport.failed and owns no httpStatus property.

entries.providerBehavior: A GitLab throttled response is built without a structured status.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: read-delivery-request resolves to tracker.transport.failed because the status is structurally absent.

entries.providerBehavior: A GitLab 2xx body that does not decode is a status-less payload failure.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: read-delivery-request resolves to tracker.transport.failed and the difference is recorded as failure-classification.

entries.providerBehavior: A GitLab pipeline read declares no page bound and reports no page count.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: read-pipeline-run returns a bare item list with no declared bound and no reported count, so the family is recorded through pagination-model.
